combine (`a || b`).rule: plan_branch_markers: `every CondBr condition is a MARKED RESULT of its own block` (the `param_cond`/`match_bool` tripwire). `combine`'s condition is the bare param `%1`.
combine (`a || b`).lane_K_counterexample_REPRODUCED_AT_HEAD: `pc(a,x,y){ if a {x} else {y} }` and `mb(c,x,y){ match c { true=>x, false=>y } }` lower to trust-ir that is IDENTICAL block for block, instruction for instruction, edge arg for edge arg — `bb0: condbr %0, bb1, bb2 ; bb1: br bb3(%1) ; bb2: br bb3(%2) ; bb3(%3): ret %3` — and the ONLY differing token is the `#loc` of the `if`/`match` keyword, i.e. where the two functions sit in the file. Built gives `pc` TWO markers plus an empty else-entry and gives `mb` ZERO markers plus a `falseEdge` candidate and an unreachable. So the rule is not conservatism: it is a genuine module-indistinguishability, and admitting the pair would cost `mb`'s existing flip.
combine (`a || b`).BUT_THE_SUGAR_IS_SEPARABLE: `a || b` and `a && b` are NOT in that pair. MEASURED on f8c.rs: `or1`/`an1` carry the synthesized constant at the SAME `#loc` as the `CondBr` itself (8:39/8:39 and 10:39/10:39) and emit the else-arm block FIRST; `if1` (`if a {true} else {b}`), `ma1` (`match a {true=>true,false=>b}`) and `if2` all carry the constant at its own literal position (4:46, 6:57, 12:57), distinct from the `CondBr`'s. `if1` and `ma1` remain byte-indistinguishable from EACH OTHER, so both must stay refused — but the `||`/`&&` desugar is a Module-visible signature and `combine` can be admitted on it without touching them.
combine (`a || b`).verdict: TAKEABLE, not built here. Costs: one narrowed clause in plan_branch_markers' condition rule, a plan-gated condition temp for a bare-param condition in the CondBr emitter, and the matching `live`+`assign` in predict_from's CondBr arm. The trampoline is already minted.

clamp_u32.rule: plan_branch_markers: `results are LEFTMOST in every operand list`, which names `clamp_u32` in its own source, verbatim.
clamp_u32.measured: built bb0 is `StorageLive(_2)[result]; StorageLive(_3)[operand0]; _3 = copy _1; StorageLive(_4)[operand1]; _4 = const MAX as u64; _2 = Gt(move _3, move _4)` — markers at .0, .0, .1. The trust-ir is `%2 = const u32 MAX; %3 = zext %2 to u64; %4 = icmp ugt %0, %3`, so the shim's LINEAR walk emits the cast's own statement before it ever reaches the icmp's operand slots and mints the two temps in the wrong order.
clamp_u32.verdict: an operand-ORDER wall, ORTHOGONAL to blocks. Takeable in principle by delaying a marked result's defining statement to its use site and minting operand temps left to right; that is a widening of the operand-temp discipline, not a block-graph change.

scopes_firewall_verdict.verdict: CORRECT — not stale — for both bodies, and REDUNDANT: each is refused twice over.
scopes_firewall_verdict.why: `env::native_reducers_bitvec::to_signed` binds `let half = 1u128 << (w - 1);` and `env::native_reducers_sint::to_signed` binds `let sign_bit = 1u64 << (bits - 1);`. The firewall's documented meaning is exactly `the producer opened a let-visibility scope`, and that is TRUE of both — a real source `let`, with the named binding local and the `FakeRead` the instruction stream cannot see. This is not the destructuring-param case the module docs name as the firewall's heuristic gap; that case is a body the firewall LETS THROUGH and the oracle then refuses, which is a false negative of the firewall, not a false positive.
scopes_firewall_verdict.second_independent_refusal: both bodies carry an EARLY RETURN (`return 0;` / `return val as i64;`), i.e. a SECOND `Inst::Return`, which `plan_branch_markers` refuses on its own line (`exactly one Return`). Consuming the scope table would therefore not be enough; the early-return shape has to land too — and that shape is F7's harder half, measured below.
scopes_firewall_verdict.so_the_firewall_costs_nothing_here: lifting it would move neither body.

perturbation_sw_tramp.what_it_does: `-Ztrust-sat-perturb=sw-tramp` MOVES one match-candidate trampoline off the plan's first non-last candidate and onto the LAST candidate's edge, which the plan never puts one on. The TOTAL is unchanged, so every later `new_block` index is unchanged and the marker LAW — which models the allocation, not the placement — stays green; an empty `Goto` on either edge is the same program, so the derived-MIR semantic channel cannot refuse it either. The ONLY channel that can is `canon_markers`, which walks the RAW CFG and therefore sees the join one fine block early.
